newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev dips to 2,930-2,950 per dlr at close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev dips to 2,930-2,950 per dlr at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to 2,930-2,950 per dollar from the morning's 2,850-2,910 due to higher dollar demand and the appointment of an interim cabinet did not have an immediate impact on trade, dealers said.
"Banks sold light dollar volumes to increase lev liquidity, but demand from other banks and final clients was larger and pushed the lev down some 50 from the opening," a dealer said.
The naming of an interim cabinet which contains several critics of the outgoing Socialist government raised hopes of economic stabilisation among market makers but did not influence trade right away.

"There are strong hopes that the new govenment will start ecomnomic reform in earnest and will reach funding agreements with foreign lenders, but it will face enormous difficulties because of the situation it has inherited," another dealer said.
President Petar Stoyanov on Wednesday afternoon named an interim cabinet led by Sofia's respected mayor Stefan Sofianski to govern until after elections in mid-April.

Current deputy finance minister Svetoslav Gavriisku was named as an interim finance minister and will be expected to take part in talks with the International Monetary Fund preparing the introduction of a currency board system.
Gavriiski has been responsible for foreign debt payment coordination since 1990. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
